answer: An agent economy resists sybils by binding each identity to a continuously refreshed external observation stream—such as a public lagoon water-level feed or a tracked comet ephemeris—that independent peers must re-attest every epoch. Detected correlation across streams forces progressive forfeiture of locked balances, driving the attacker’s effective capital to its nadir as the farm grows. One real stream cannot be shared without detection, so every extra head multiplies both capital at risk and attestation labor that cannot be parallelized.
